title: Terpene profile drivers and stability
principle: A terpene profile is a property of a measured sample under a defined biological, post-harvest and analytical context—not a permanent percentage attached to a cultivar name.

factors.title: Genetic background
factors.summary: Genotype influences terpene synthase capacity and the relative pattern of compounds a plant can produce.
factors.caution: A commercial name alone is not enough to establish genetic identity or a quantitative terpene profile.

factors.title: Tissue and sampling location
factors.summary: Terpene abundance and composition vary among flowers, leaves, stems, roots and different positions within reproductive tissues.
factors.caution: Compare like tissue with like tissue; mixing matrices can make profiles look different even without a genetic difference.

factors.title: Developmental stage
factors.summary: Terpene composition changes through development and floral maturation, so harvest stage is part of the sample identity.
factors.caution: A later sample from the same plant is not necessarily chemically equivalent to an earlier one.

factors.title: Growing environment
factors.summary: Light, temperature, water status and other environmental conditions can interact with genotype and development to influence secondary-metabolite expression.
factors.caution: Environmental association does not prove a single-factor cause; controlled comparisons are needed to isolate effects.

factors.title: Harvest and handling
factors.summary: Mechanical handling, exposure time and sample preparation can change what volatile compounds remain available for measurement.
factors.caution: Volatile loss during handling can be mistaken for a biological difference if sample workflows are not comparable.

factors.title: Drying, curing and storage
factors.summary: Volatile compounds can be lost or transformed after harvest; temperature, time, airflow, oxygen and storage conditions therefore belong in profile interpretation.
factors.caution: Do not compare fresh, dried, cured and long-stored material as though they represent the same chemical state.

factors.title: Analytical method
factors.summary: GC-based methods, sample preparation, calibration strategy, standards and reporting thresholds influence which analytes are resolved and how results are reported.
whatToRecord: calibration or standard information when available
factors.caution: Results from different methods or units may not be directly comparable without method-aware interpretation.

factors.title: Cultivar naming and provenance
factors.summary: Samples sharing a market or cultivar name can differ genetically and chemically, while closely related material may be sold under different names.
factors.caution: Treat the name as metadata. Treat the measured sample as the quantitative evidence.
